quote.citation: 2013 July-August, Catherine Clabby, “Focus on Everything”, in American Scientist:
quote.text: Not long ago, it was difficult to produce photographs of tiny creatures with every part in focus. That’s because the lenses that are excellent at magnifying tiny subjects produce a narrow depth of field. A photo processing technique called focus stacking has changed that.

quote.citation: 2005 June 28, “Racing diary: In the shake-up”, in The Telegraph‎[1]:
quote.text: By this stage, Goof was clearly warming to his theme and, as they flashed past the post together, he reported that it was a photo. "And I don't know or care who won the photo," he concluded.

definitions.definition: (informal) A digital picture of any kind.

quote.citation: [1956] 1992 ed., The Complete Lyrics of Cole Porter [2]
quote.text: What fun to be photoed together, / What luck for a break so opportune. / Oh, what a lark / To be posed in the park / Underneath the adolescent crescent of the moon.
He even had himself photoed helping to hold one of the fire-hose.

quote.citation: 2000, Salman Rushdie, The Ground Beneath Her Feet [4]
quote.text: Always photoing exits. What are all these ways out but rehearsals for his own?
